title: Deploying Containerized Apps on AKS
description: Deploy and manage containerized microservices on Azure Kubernetes Service.

data.text: You have 5 microservices (API Gateway, Auth, Orders, Inventory, Notifications) running in Docker containers. You need orchestration, auto-scaling, service discovery, and rolling updates. Which Azure compute option should you choose?
Choose **Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)** for container orchestration. It provides managed Kubernetes, auto-scaling, built-in CI/CD integration, and supports complex microservice architectures.

data.title: Azure CLI - Create AKS Cluster
data.code:
# Create AKS cluster with managed identity
az aks create \
  --resource-group 'rg-microservices' \
  --name 'aks-microservices' \
  --node-count 3 \
  --enable-addons monitoring \
  --generate-ssh-keys \
  --enable-managed-identity

# Get credentials
az aks get-credentials --resource-group 'rg-microservices' --name 'aks-microservices'

# Deploy application
kubectl apply -f k8s-manifests/

data.title: Kubernetes Deployment Manifest
data.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: orders-api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: orders-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: orders-api
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: orders-api
        image: myregistry.azurecr.io/orders-api:v1
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"

data.text: **AKS** provides managed Kubernetes without the overhead of managing the control plane. It integrates with Azure Container Registry, Azure Monitor, and Azure DevOps. The Kubernetes ecosystem offers the richest set of orchestration features.
